html:
The Shoshone-Bannock Tribes are a nation of Northern Shoshone and Bannock people based on the Fort Hall Reservation in south-east Idaho, along the Snake River. The Shoshone speak a Numic language of the Uto-Aztecan family; the Bannock spoke a Northern Paiute dialect and lived among them. They hunted bison, fished salmon and gathered camas roots, and took up horses early, in the 1700s.

Sacagawea, who travelled with the Lewis and Clark Expedition, was a Lemhi Shoshone. The Oregon Trail crossed their land, and Fort Hall itself began as a fur trading post on it. The Fort Bridger Treaty of 1868 set up the reservation; hunger and settlers' livestock on the camas grounds set off the Bannock War of 1878. In 1907 the Lemhi Shoshone were moved to Fort Hall as well.
